findings.name: general appearance
findings.result: Well-nourished and well-developed; sitting comfortably, in no distress.

findings.name: eye examination
findings.result: Pupils equal, round and reactive to light and accommodation.

findings.name: fundoscopic examination
findings.result: Normal; no arteriovenous nicking, hemorrhages or exudates.

findings.name: neck examination
findings.result: No carotid bruits; no jugular venous distension.

findings.name: lung auscultation
findings.result: Breath sounds clear on both sides.

findings.name: heart examination
findings.result: Apical impulse not displaced; regular rate and rhythm; normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, rubs or gallops.

findings.name: abdominal examination
findings.result: Soft, not distended, not tender; bowel sounds present in all four quadrants; no bruits; no enlargement of the liver or spleen.

findings.name: extremities examination
findings.result: No edema; no skin breakdown; dorsalis pedis pulses 2+ and symmetric.

findings.name: reflexes
findings.result: Knee reflexes present, 2+ and symmetric; ankle reflexes absent on both sides.

findings.name: sensation
findings.result: Both feet, in a stocking distribution: loss of sharp and dull sensation (pinprick), vibration sense and position sense. Soft touch intact in both legs.

evidence: Episodes of palpitations and diaphoresis that resolve with drinking orange juice
Constant numbness and tingling in feet bilaterally
Exam: Diminished pinprick sensation on plantar surfaces
Loss of erection for 2 years with absence of early-morning erection

other_considerations.note: A distal sensorimotor polyneuropathy with painful leg paresthesias, caused by alcohol or associated nutritional deficiencies (e.g., thiamine, B vitamins); he drinks whiskey on weekends.
Myeloma or other paraproteinemias must be ruled out in a patient with peripheral neuropathy.
Uremia can cause a sensory peripheral neuropathy, including in diabetic patients.
Can be associated with peripheral neuropathy and other neurologic symptoms.
Polyarteritis nodosa, rheumatoid arthritis and other vasculitides can cause peripheral neuropathy and are detected with ESR, ANCA, RF and anti-CCP antibodies.

x015: Source reads '6 Babinski bilaterally'; the symbol before 'Babinski' is garbled, so the direction (upgoing or downgoing) is unknown.
x016: The SP simulates loss of sharp/dull, vibration and position sense in both feet; the note exam records only diminished plantar pinprick with intact vibration and position sense. The simulated finding is the result (CONVERSION.md); soft touch, which the SP notes do not mention, is from the note.

leakage.reason: The patient was told his erection problem is caused by diabetes, which points to organic (diabetic) erectile dysfunction, gold diagnosis #3. It is scripted patient content and is kept.

source_issues: patient_note_history is empty in the source file: the raw sheet's note heading is 'Patient Note' without a colon, so the parser missed it. The full note (HPI, ROS, meds, PMH, SH, FH) is present in raw_opening and was used for checking; f009 cites it as 'note'.
p007: HbA1c result '7.210' is garbled (probably OCR); the note gives 'Last HbA1c 6 months ago was 7%'. Recorded as about 7% with a flag.
e009: '6 Babinski bilaterally' - the '6' is a garbled symbol (probably a circled minus or plus); direction not stated; recorded as 'Result not documented' with a flag (x015).

Contradiction between SP notes and the note exam: the SP is told to show loss of sharp/dull, vibration and position sense in both feet (stocking distribution), but the note exam records only diminished pinprick on the plantar surfaces and intact soft touch, vibration and position sense. The simulated loss is the sensation result (x016).
p034: alcohol amount is not given; the answer trails off ('only on the weekend...').
Erectile problem duration: script 'One or 2 years' (p040); the note and gold say 2 years.

p012 asks about dizziness and confusion among hypoglycemic symptoms, and p015 about headaches, dizziness and weakness; the answers address only sweating/racing heart and foot tingling/numbness, so these items are neither confirmed nor denied by the script (the note's 'ROS: Negative except as above' is generic and was not used to create denials).
p038 ('Are you currently sexually active?') is not answered directly; the patient describes a performance problem instead.
gold_additional_diagnosis starts with a general sentence about non-diabetic neuropathy causes (not a diagnosis); 'thiamine and vitamin B' is probably truncated (e.g., B12).
Gold #3 'History of alcohol use' rests on weekend whiskey with no stated amount.
notes: Per a later policy update (which overrides the GUIDE.md Babinski example wording), env findings carry no review commentary: an undirected Babinski is recorded as 'Result not documented' and the reason is in the record's flags.
The chief complaint is a visit reason (diabetes checkup), used as the opening fact (f001); the last visit 6 months ago (v1 f001) is f002.

Diabetes and its management (insulin, monitoring, HbA1c, eye and foot care) are medical_history or medication; the symptoms elicited (sweating/racing-heart spells, foot numbness/tingling, erectile problem) are symptoms.
The sweating/racing-heart spells are described in the patient's words without the label 'hypoglycemia' to avoid naming the rank-1 diagnosis.
'I don't even wake up with erections anymore' is coded as a present symptom (the erection problem extends to waking, f040), per guide rule 2.
p003 (no medication side effects) is recorded literally even though the sweating spells may be insulin-related.
f063 combines 'Do you smoke? Did you ever smoke in the past?' - 'No' as a never-smoker.
Conversion: the first v1 source issue is outdated for the current source inventory, whose patient_note_history now holds the note (it contains the 7% HbA1c); the quote check for f009 uses it.

Conversion: sensation follows CONVERSION.md (simulated finding wins), replacing v1's separate note and SP records (x023-x029) with one record x016; reflexes merge the matching note and SP findings (x014).

Conversion: home glucose monitoring (p005, p006) is a parent f005 with frequency, usual and latest readings as children; NPH insulin (p002, p026) is f048 with its dose as a child; the eye-doctor finding is a child of the visit (f011); the erection problem (v1 f056, p038-p040) is a parent f038 with duration (f039) and waking erections (f040) as children.

Conversion: gold aliases leave out plain 'hypoglycemia', 'erectile dysfunction' and 'peripheral neuropathy' because they are broader than the reference diagnoses (CONVERSION.md); a scorer may want to treat them as partial matches.
